classification.difficultyReason: Construct labelled diagrams from prose and combine isosceles properties with angle calculations.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Let $\triangle ABC$ be isosceles, with $AB=AC$. Produce $BC$ to $D$, and let $\angle ACD=124^\circ$. Draw a diagram and find $\angle ABC$, giving reasons.

answer.short:
$\angle ABC=56^\circ$.

The base angles are equal, and $\angle ACB=180^\circ-124^\circ$.
answer.worked:
Angles on the straight line $BCD$ add to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}\angle ACB&=180^\circ-124^\circ\\\angle ACB&=56^\circ\end{align*}$$
Since $AB=AC$, the base angles of $\triangle ABC$ are equal. Hence $\angle ABC=\angle ACB=56^\circ$.

spec.description: Completed labelled isosceles triangle with BC produced to D, equal-side ticks, exterior 124-degree angle and the required 56-degree angle at B.
spec.mathematics: AB=AC; B,C,D are collinear in that order; exterior angle ACD is 124 degrees.

children.label: b
children.prompt: $P$ and $Q$ are points on a circle with centre $O$ such that $\angle POQ=48^\circ$. Draw a diagram and calculate the size of $\angle OPQ$.

answer.short:
$\angle OPQ=66^\circ$.

$OP=OQ$ because they are radii, so the two base angles are equal.
answer.worked:
$OP=OQ$ because they are radii of the same circle. Therefore $\angle OPQ=\angle OQP$ by the base-angle property of an isosceles triangle.
$$\begin{align*}\angle OPQ+\angle OQP&=180^\circ-48^\circ\\\angle OPQ+\angle OQP&=132^\circ\\\angle OPQ&=132^\circ\div2\\\angle OPQ&=66^\circ\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Completed circle with centre O, points P and Q on its circumference, two equal radii, chord PQ, central 48-degree angle and required 66-degree angle at P.
spec.mathematics: OP=OQ; angle POQ=48 degrees; angle OPQ=66 degrees.
